asia.name: Asia
asia.intro: From warming cups of chai to colourful rice bowls, discover a few favourites from across Asia.

Simmer ginger and cardamom in water. Add tea, then milk and sugar; bring to a gentle simmer and strain.
Whisk sifted matcha with a little warm water until smooth. Top with warmed, frothed milk.
Ripe mango, plain yogurt, milk, cardamom
Blend mango and yogurt with a splash of milk. Add cardamom and serve chilled.
black tea, sugar, condensed or evaporated milk
Brew strong tea, sweeten, pour over ice and finish with milk.
tea, tapioca pearls, sugar, milk or non-dairy alternative

cooked rice, malted barley, water, sugar

Singapore; popular in Malaysia and Brunei
rose cordial or syrup, milk, ice
Stir rose syrup into chilled milk and serve cold.
Simmer or steep roasted barley, strain and serve hot or chilled.

Steep coffee grounds directly in a cup and let them settle before drinking.
Soak and grind soybeans with water, cook the mixture and strain.

Roast semolina, temper aromatics, add water and cook until soft.
Ferment the batter, swirl it in a small deep pan and cook until the center sets and edges crisp.
Moisten rice flour, layer with coconut and steam in a cylindrical mould.
rice, water or stock, pork floss, pickled mustard greens
Simmer rice until porridge-like and add the toppings.
sticky rice, tablea or cocoa, sugar, milk
Simmer rice with chocolate and sugar until thick, then serve with milk.
Rest the dough, stretch paired strips and deep-fry until puffed and golden.

South Asia

Dolsot bibimbap
Korea
rice, seasoned vegetables, gochujang, sesame oil, egg
Arrange toppings over rice in a hot stone bowl and serve sizzling.

Thailand

Stir-fry noodles with sauce, prawns, egg and other toppings.

Shoyu ramen
Japan

Vietnam

Bulgogi
Korea

europe.name: Europe
europe.intro: Explore café drinks, comforting breakfasts and familiar meals from European kitchens.

Red wine, orange, lemon, other fruit, optional sugar or brandy

africa.name: Africa
africa.intro: Meet fragrant teas, hearty grains and warming stews from a few of Africa’s many food traditions.
